instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Nowadays, almost everyone is on some type of social media platform. After all, it is an entertaining way to do things like watch our friends’ videos, learn new recipes or look at cute animal clips. Although being this connected has many positive effects, there is also a flip side to social media.

atoms.text: Studies have confirmed that using social media may be extremely addictive, especially for children and teenagers (1). One example of this addiction may be reflected in users’ screen times: children and teenagers are said to be on their phones for up to 7 hours a day. Confirmation in the form of hearts or a thumbs up may be messing with our brains’ chemistry. Our human brains appear to be craving the next dopamine kick.

atoms.text:
Social media is part of our current reality, which is why we shouldn’t try to stop using it at all costs. When used in the right way, using social media can even have positive effects - like staying informed. Instead of entirely banning it, we should be more aware of its addictive sides and the effects this may have on children and teenagers.

atoms.a: What is the author trying to convince the reader to do?
b: ++To be more aware of the effects social media may have on children and teenagers’ mental health.
To be aware of the positive effects social media has.

atoms.a: Is the author’s stance towards social media more positive or negative?
What evidence does the author share to try to convince the reader of social media’s addictive sides?
b: ++The amount of time children and teenagers spend on their phones.
Watching friends’ videos and cute animal videos.
That social media is more entertaining than reading a book.

atoms.a: Why does the author mention the amount of time children and teenagers spend on their phones?
b: ++To show the highly addictive qualities of using social media.
To show how everyone is on some type of social media platform.
To follow up on how much time adults spend on their phones.

atoms.a: What might the reader do if they took what the author said to heart?
b: ++They may reflect on their own social media choices.
Watch friends’ videos and cute animal videos.
Realise that social media is more entertaining than reading a book.
